notes: CHK-019 is the weak point. It uses a negedge-sampled comparison (outputs at falling i_clk vs. just before the next rising edge), which catches mid-cycle changes only if they occur between those two points. It uses an `initial` block (no delay) and a combinational `always` block that are not needed, and I did not verify that it compiles in Verilator 5. The unused `chg_*`, `prev_*` and `post_ok` signals can be deleted. The 1->0 reset-edge exception is covered only because the assertion is disabled during reset. CHK-020 to CHK-022 use a model that tracks the transfer from handshake A (cpha captured at A, MISO shifted at the sample edges, byte pushed at A+16*D) and a queue of depth up to 3 so overflow is visible. Nothing was compiled or simulated.
